transcript.text: Hi everyone, thanks for making time. As part of the normal approval routine for the peer-feedback pilot, I'd like to do a round-robin check-in with the project team member and our HR program partner before I issue the final plan. I want to make sure we're all aligned on the operating safeguards, especially given the tense exchanges that have come up in recent product retrospectives. Before we get into specifics, I'd like to hear from each of you on a couple of things: first, what concerns or risks do you see with running this pilot as currently described, and second, what safeguards do you think we need to have in place to make sure this doesn't replicate the same friction we've been seeing in those retrospective sessions?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Thanks Elena. I'm glad we're doing this check-in before finalizing. I have some concerns about the current pilot description. As it stands, the proposal mentions facilitated discussion, ordinary participation, and a review after the pilot — but it doesn't specify the detailed safeguards, and I think that gap is significant given what's been happening in our retros. I've observed a pattern of dismissive interruptions across our last three retrospectives that's affecting people's willingness to speak openly. I also have specific concerns that some colleagues may not feel safe contributing in a group format at all, and we need to account for that before we put a peer-feedback pilot in front of everyone. Rather than just flag the concern abstractly, I'd like to share exactly what I've observed so we can design the right safeguards. I'd like to reveal that now if it's helpful.
